messages:
sara: Hey team — hitting a recurring SSE problem in prod. Streams stop delivering the final object; the JSON is truncated and finish_reason is missing. Seen ~15 user reports in the last hour. :eyes:

devon: Can you paste a raw capture and the request you used? Is this only on Hosted or also Dedicated/private?

sara: Hosted only so far. Raw curl capture (sanitized):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=rw-1"
```
Stream payload excerpt:
```
data: {"id":"tok_1","delta":"Hello"}
data: {"id":"tok_1","delta":" world"}
data: {"id":"tok_1","delta":"!"}
data: {"id":"tok_1","delta":"Final chunk start..."}
data: {"id":"tok_1","delta":"incomplete"
```
(note: last line ends abruptly, no closing brace, no finish_reason, connection stays open for ~200ms then client reconnects)

ingrid: Any proxy/edge 401s or auth-handshake logs around that time? Reconnects often correlate with token rotation.

sara: Yes — client rotated its token and attempted to resume the stream. Client sends a resume header: `X-Resume-Session: sess_abc;offset=1024` and then immediately opens a new SSE connection. Server-side we see the resume request, but the output that comes back lacks the terminal sentinel.

devon: That suggests a routing fallback during resume. If the resume request routed to a different runtime (smaller model or standby node) it might not replay the final buffered suffix or append the terminal object. Do you have control-plane route logs?

ops_jamal: I pulled control-plane traces for the window: there was a routing fallback to standby cluster-3 at 2026-03-15T14:02:11Z with reason `capacity_spill`. The stream session was attempted to be resumed there. I also see a runtime warning `stream_end_sentinel_missing` right after the resume. Filed an internal ticket.

sara: Repro steps I used locally:
1) Start a streaming request with long output (seq > 1024).
2) mid-stream, rotate auth token on client and immediately call resume with header `X-Resume-Session` and same session id.
3) observe that the resumed SSE ends with a partial JSON object (truncated) and client never receives a finish_reason.
Node fetch snippet I used:
```js
const res = await fetch(url, {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${shortLived}`, 'X-Resume-Session': 'sess_abc;offset=1024' },
  signal
});
res.body.on('data', chunk => console.log(chunk.toString()));
```

devon: Thanks — that matches the hypothesis. Short-term mitigations for customers: 1) set client to re-request the final document via non-streaming (sync) completion endpoint if finish_reason is absent; 2) pin session routing using `X-Session-Pin` to avoid fallback during resume; 3) add a short client-side backoff and then a resume attempt that includes `last_event_id`.

ingrid: Any sign of billing or quota enforcement cutting connections? Even a soft 429 could cause abrupt stream termination.

sara: We did see a handful of 429s earlier in the hour for the same tenant, but the captured SSE did not include an HTTP 429 for that particular request. I can attach the full request/response logs to the ticket.

support-bot: Incident created: IN-2026-457 — internal link: https://internal.redwood/incident/IN-2026-457. Tagging eng-runtime and infra.

ops_jamal: Notes from initial triage: reproduced on staging by forcing an auth rotation + resume header while simultaneously triggering capacity spill routing. Root cause: resume flow didn't guarantee terminal sentinel on model/routing fallback. Plan: ensure runtime appends terminal object on any resume or emits an explicit finish event even when replayed from a different node. Will schedule hotfix for the resume handler (PR target: today).

devon: Also logging action items: add metrics for `resume_count` vs `successful_finish`, add an alert for `missing_finish_reason_rate > 0.1%`, and add a diagnostic flag that dumps the last 2KB of the streamed buffer on resume.

ops_jamal: Workaround for support to advise customers now: attempt a follow-up request to the sync completion endpoint with the same prompt and session id to retrieve final tokens; enable `session_pin` if you need strict routing.

sara: I've messaged the affected customer with the above mitigations and asked for the full capture. I'll paste their capture once available. Thanks team. :pray:

devon: Great — keep this thread updated. If you get the capture, include the TCP-level bytes and any edge proxy logs (Fastly / CDN) so we can rule out mid-stream buffering.

sara: Will do. Marking as escalated until hotfix is deployed.
